[reflective] A man insulted Jesus behind His back. Jesus complimented him to his face.

[serious] Philip told Nathanael the news: the Messiah — Jesus, of Nazareth. Nathanael's answer:

<speaker name="nathanael">[questioning] "Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?"</speaker>

[serious] Philip did not argue — he invited. Jesus spoke first:

<speaker name="jesus">[emphasized] "Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!"</speaker>

[serious] Nathanael asked:

<speaker name="nathanael">[questioning] "Whence knowest thou me?"</speaker>

[serious] Jesus answered:

<speaker name="jesus">[quietly][deliberate] "Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee."</speaker>

[reflective] A moment only heaven had seen — named. The doubt did not fade. It fell. Nathanael said:

<speaker name="nathanael">[awe] "Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art the King of Israel."</speaker>

[serious] And Jesus went further:

<speaker name="jesus">[slow][reflective][awe] "Thou shalt see greater things than these... Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man."</speaker>

[reflective] That is Jacob's ladder — the one Jesus said He is, standing open, permanently.

[reflective] He is not offended by honest questions. He already sees you, under your fig tree.

[quietly] Come and see.
